title: The well-pleaded complaint rule
summary: The well-pleaded complaint rule looks to the plaintiff’s own claim for federal-question jurisdiction. A federal defense anticipated in the complaint ordinarily does not make a state-law claim arise under federal law.
notes: The rule differs from the breadth of Article III and from the merits of a federal defense. Specialized removal doctrines discussed in the notes require separate treatment.

sections.Meaning: The well-pleaded complaint rule looks to the plaintiff’s own claim for federal-question jurisdiction. A federal defense anticipated in the complaint ordinarily does not make a state-law claim arise under federal law.
sections.How to work through the question: State what the plaintiff must establish to obtain relief. Remove predictions about the defendant’s federal defense and the plaintiff’s response to that defense, then examine the remaining claim. Mottley’s contract-enforcement claim illustrates the distinction.
